claims.text: The starting material is an Al0.1Co1.5CrFeMnNi high-entropy-alloy coating.
The starting coating has a mixed FCC/BCC structure.
The starting coating is in the as-cast state.
Aging at 700°C for 24 hours will introduce coherent L12-structured precipitates.
The precipitate-matrix interface is the structural mediator governing creep resistance.
Coherent L12 precipitates will strongly obstruct dislocation movement.
Obstruction of dislocation movement by the precipitates will enhance creep resistance.
The precipitate-matrix interface will act as a sink for dislocations.
Dislocation absorption at the interface will reduce the overall dislocation density.
Reduced dislocation density will promote a more stable microstructure.
At 600°C and 200 MPa sustained stress, the aged coating will have a steady-state creep rate at least 30% lower than that of the as-cast coating.
The creep response is predicted specifically under continuous loading at 600°C and a constant stress of 200 MPa.
The magnitude of creep resistance may depend on the aging conditions and resulting microstructure.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least a 30% reduction in steady-state creep rate, but the falsification rule rejects the hypothesis only if there is no improvement. An improvement smaller than 30% would violate the quantitative prediction while not meeting the stated falsification criterion.
